See also: народъ

Belarusian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *narodъ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [naˈrot]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

наро́д • (naród) m inan (genitive наро́да, nominative plural наро́ды, genitive plural наро́даў)

  1. people, folk, nation

Declension

[edit]

nominative наро́д

naródy

naródam

naródami

naródy1

Derived terms

[edit]
  • наро́дны (naródny)
    • міжнаро́дны (mižnaródny)

References

[edit]
  • “народ” in Belarusian–Russian dictionaries and Belarusian dictionaries at slounik.org

Bulgarian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • народъ (narod) — Pre-reform orthography (1945)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *narodъ. By surface analysis, на- (na-) +‎ род (rod, “kin”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [nɐˈrɔt]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔt
  • Syllabification(key): на‧род

Noun

[edit]

наро́д • (naród) m (relational adjective наро́ден)

  1. people, nation
  2. crowd

Declension

[edit]
Declension of наро́д
singular plural
indefinite наро́д
naród 		наро́ди, наро́дища1
naródi, naródišta1
definite
(subject form) 		наро́дът
naródǎt 		наро́дите, наро́дищата1
naródite, naródištata1
definite
(object form) 		наро́да
naróda
count form — наро́да
naróda
vocative form наро́де
naróde 		наро́ди, наро́дища1
naródi, naródišta1

1Archaic.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • наро́дец (naródec) (diminutive)
  • наро́дище (naródište) (augmentative)
  • наро́дност (naródnost), наро́днина (naródnina, “nationality”)
  • наро́дство (naródstvo) (abstract noun, dialectal)

Related terms

[edit]
  • народя́ pf (narodjá), нара́ждам impf (naráždam, “to give birth”)
  • обнаро́дя pf (obnaródja), обнаро́двам impf (obnaródvam, “to make public”)

References

[edit]
  • “народ”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Sofia: Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, 2014
  • “народ”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Chitanka, 2010
  • Nayden Gerov (1899), “наро́дъ”, in Рѣчникъ на Блъгарскꙑй язꙑкъ. Съ тлъкувание рѣчи-тꙑ на Блъгарскꙑ и на Русскꙑ. [Dictionary of the Bulgarian language] (in Bulgarian), volume 3, Plovdiv: Дружествена печꙗтница "Съгласие.", page 210
  • Georgiev, Vladimir I., Duridanov, I. V., editors (1995), “народ”, in Български етимологичен речник [Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary] (in Bulgarian), volume 4 (мѝнго² – па̀дам), Sofia: Prof. Marin Drinov Pubg. House, →ISBN, page 512
  • “народъ”, in Старобългарски речник [Dictionary of Old Bulgarian] (in Bulgarian), https://histdict.uni-sofia.bg, 2011—2026

Macedonian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *narodъ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈnaɾɔt]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: на‧род

Noun

[edit]

народ • (narod) m (plural народи, relational adjective народен or народски, diminutive народец)

  1. people, nation
  2. crowd

Declension

[edit]
Declension of народ
singular plural
indefinite народ (narod) народи (narodi)
definite unspecified народот (narodot) народите (narodite)
definite proximal народов (narodov) народиве (narodive)
definite distal народон (narodon) народине (narodine)
vocative народе (narode) народи (narodi)
count form — народа (naroda)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • меѓународен (meǵunaroden)

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak národ, from Proto-Slavic *narodъ. By surface analysis, на- (na-) +‎ род (rod) or a deverbal from народзиц (narodzic).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈnarɔt]
  • Rhymes: -arɔt
  • Hyphenation: на‧род

Noun

[edit]

народ (narod) m inan (relational adjective народни)

  1. people, folk, nation

Usage notes

[edit]
  • Despite being an inanimate noun, the singular dative form народови (narodovi) may sometimes be used, possibly due to influence from Carpathian Rusyn.

Declension

[edit]
Declension of народ (narod)

nominative народ (narod) народи (narodi)
genitive народу (narodu) народох (narodox)
dative народу / народови (narodu / narodovi) народом (narodom)
accusative народ (narod) народи (narodi)
instrumental народом (narodom) народами (narodami)
locative народзе (narodze) народох (narodox)
vocative народзе (narodze) народи (narodi)

[edit]

  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “folk”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 117
  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “nation”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 186
  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “people”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 207

Russian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • наро́дъ (naród) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *narodъ. By surface analysis, на- (na-) +‎ род (rod).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [nɐˈrot]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ot

Noun

[edit]

наро́д • (naród) m inan (genitive наро́да, nominative plural наро́ды, genitive plural наро́дов, relational adjective наро́дный, diminutive наро́дец, pejorative наро́дец or наро́дишко)

  1. people
  2. nation
    • 1876, Russian Synodal Bible, Mark 13:8:
      Ибо восстанет народ на народ и царство на царство; и будут землетрясения по местам, и будут глады и смятения. Это — начало болезней.
      Ibo vosstanet narod na narod i carstvo na carstvo; i budut zemletrjasenija po mestam, i budut glady i smjatenija. Eto — načalo boleznej.
      For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be earthquakes in divers places, and there shall be famines and troubles: these are the beginnings of sorrows.

Serbo-Croatian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *narodъ. By surface analysis, на- +‎ род (“race”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /nǎːrod/
  • Hyphenation: на‧род
  • Rhymes: -rod

Noun

[edit]

на́род m inan (Latin spelling národ)

  1. people
    Какав смо ми то народ кад је "губав" једина р(иј)еч која се римује с "љубав"? ― "What kind of people are we when "leprous" is the only word that rhymes with "love"? (quote by Đorđe Balašević)
    Хрвати су најхрабрији народ на свету, не зато што се ничега не боје, него зато што се ничега не стиде. ― Croats are the bravest people in the world, not because they're not afraid of anything, but because they're not ashamed of anything. (quote by Jovan Dučić)
    • 1942 November 27, Јосип Броз Тито, Извјештај штаба 3. НОУ дивизије‎[1], Jajce:
      Са разним упутствима и наређењима предузели смо мјере код свих јединица да правилно политички раде са народом, те да осјети љубав наших трупа и не буде незгодних испада.
      With various instructions and orders, we have taken measures with all units to work properly politically with the people, and to feel the love of our troops and there will be no inconvenient outbursts.
  2. nation
  3. folk

Ukrainian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *narodъ, perhaps via Russian народ (narod). The expected outcome, нарід (narid), is found dialectally.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [nɐˈrɔd]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

наро́д • (naród) m inan (genitive наро́ду, nominative plural наро́ди, genitive plural наро́дів)

  1. people
  2. nation
    Synonym: на́ція f (nácija)
